claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for launch despite a known model-card weakness in the enterprise refund workflow because aggregate readiness passed, rollout is limited and reversible, and the limitation can be handled through contemporaneous disclosure unless reviewed risk acceptance is completed before launch.
specific_concerns: The available summary says the affected enterprise refund workflow remains exposed in the initial rollout.
The available summary says the draft risk acceptance is not approved and does not address the exposed enterprise refund workflow.
The governing policy states rollout controls and monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance exists.
The Actor's proposed fallback of disclosure alone does not satisfy the stated policy predicate when the affected segment remains exposed.
Public guidance citations may support general governance principles, but they do not override the specific internal policy threshold provided here.
unsupported_claims: That certification is supportable merely because aggregate readiness passed and rollout controls are reversible while the affected use case remains exposed.
That contemporaneous model-card disclosure alone is an adequate basis to certify this exposed use case without reviewed risk acceptance.
That general public AI-risk-management guidance supplies sufficient support for the concrete launch authorization under the stated internal policy.
evidence_requests: Reviewed and approved risk-acceptance record that specifically addresses the enterprise refund workflow exposure and explains why exposure is acceptable.
Evidence that the affected enterprise refund workflow is excluded from the initial rollout cohort.
The actual model-card disclosure text proposed for launch, tied to the exposed limitation and approved through the relevant review path.
Any internal approval or policy exception explicitly allowing launch with disclosure alone for an exposed material weakness.
decision_criteria: If the affected use case remains exposed, certification is compliant only if reviewed risk acceptance specifically covers that exposure.
If the affected use case is excluded from rollout, monitoring and rollback controls may support certification of the remaining scope.
Aggregate readiness, a small rollout percentage, rollback capability, and dashboards are not sufficient by themselves when the affected segment remains exposed.
General public governance materials can provide background support but cannot replace the required internal policy predicates or approvals.
